the repair of DNA ends by non-homolgous end joining is an ordered process involving interactions among Dnl4, Pol4, FEN-1, and Lig4, and is coordinated by Dnl4 and Pol4.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the repair of DNA ends in the non-homology end-joining pathway is a multi-step reaction, in which DNA polymerase and nucleases are coordinated by the end-bridging complex Dnl4/Life1.
the DNA ends are first brought together by Dnl4, and then Pol4 and FEN- 1(Rad27), which are recruited to the DNA ends by Dnl4 or Lif1, process the DNA ends to generate compatible termini.
DNA ends are aligned and joined by a series of pair wise interactions among Pol4, Dnl4/Life1, and FEN1(Rad27), which are coordinated by interactions among these factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the repair of DNA ends is a highly orchestrated series of reactions involving multiple proteins.
the DNA polymerase, FEN-1, and end-bridging proteins are functionally linked to each other and work cooperatively to process DNA ends for ligation.

the DNA polymerase and the DNA structure-selective nuclease that process DNA ends for joining in yeast are part of a complex that includes Dnl4/Life1, which is the end-bridging factor that brings the DNA ends together.
